proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(r\ge r_0\) and suppose
\[
 \max_{m\in\mathcal E}\|S_{m,r}-\Sigma_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le a_r\le (2\kappa)^{-1}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}observed\mbox{-}conditioning}\) gives
\(\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_m)\ge\kappa^{-1}\).  Weyl's inequality, proved directly from the Rayleigh variational formula, therefore gives
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(S_{m,r})
 \ge \lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_m)-\|S_{m,r}-\Sigma_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \ge (2\kappa)^{-1}>0.
\]
Thus \(S_{m,r}\) is invertible and
\(\|S_{m,r}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\kappa\).  Since
\(S^{-1}-\Sigma^{-1}=S^{-1}(\Sigma-S)\Sigma^{-1}\),
\[
 \|S_{m,r}^{-1}-\Theta_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le (2\kappa)a_r\kappa=2\kappa^2a_r.
\]
Put \(\widehat\Delta_{m,r}=S_{0,r}^{-1}-S_{m,r}^{-1}\).  By the preceding inequality and the triangle inequality,
\[
 \|\widehat\Delta_{m,r}-\Delta_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le4\kappa^2a_r,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Delta_{m,r}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le4\kappa,
 \qquad
 \|\Delta_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\kappa.
\]
The last two bounds use \(\|S_{m,r}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\kappa\) and \(\|\Theta_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa\), respectively.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}primitive\mbox{-}correlations}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat R_{m,r}-R_m
 &=\widehat\Delta_{m,r}(S_{0,r}-\Sigma_0)\widehat\Delta_{m,r}\\
 &\quad +(\widehat\Delta_{m,r}-\Delta_m)\Sigma_0\widehat\Delta_{m,r}
       +\Delta_m\Sigma_0(\widehat\Delta_{m,r}-\Delta_m).
\end{aligned}
\]
Submultiplicativity and \(\|\Sigma_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat R_{m,r}-R_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le16\kappa^2a_r+16\kappa^4a_r+8\kappa^4a_r\\
 &\le40\kappa^4a_r=e_r,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second line uses \(\kappa\ge1\).  Finally, for every \(M\subseteq[n]\), the definitions of \(R(M)\) and \(\widehat R_r(M)\) and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \|\widehat R_r(M)-R(M)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\sum_{m\in M}\|\widehat R_{m,r}-R_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le |M|e_r.
\]

Because \(A=U^{\top}G\) is invertible under \(\mathrm{ass{:}full\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}mixing}\), define
\(h_i=A^{-\top}e_i\) and \(g_i=Ae_i\).  They are dual:
\[
 h_i^{\top}g_j=e_i^{\top}A^{-1}Ae_j=\mathbf 1\{i=j\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal U_T=\operatorname{span}\{h_i:i\in T\}\) and
\(\mathcal W_S=\operatorname{span}\{h_i:i\in S\}^{\perp}\).  If \(T\subseteq S\), then \(\mathcal U_T\subseteq\mathcal W_S^{\perp}\), so
\(P_{\mathcal U_T}P_{\mathcal W_S}=0\).  Conversely, take \(i\in T\setminus S\).  Duality gives \(g_i\in\mathcal W_S\), whereas \(h_i\in\mathcal U_T\).  Testing the projector product on \(g_i/\|g_i\|_2\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|P_{\mathcal U_T}P_{\mathcal W_S}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\ge \left\|P_{\mathcal U_T}\frac{g_i}{\|g_i\|_2}\right\|_2\\
 &\ge \left|\left\langle
       \frac{h_i}{\|h_i\|_2},\frac{g_i}{\|g_i\|_2}
       \right\rangle\right|
 =\frac{1}{\|A^{-\top}e_i\|_2\|Ae_i\|_2}>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the equivalence and the stated witness bound.  Since \(U\) is an isometry from \(\mathbb R^n\) into \(\mathcal S\),
\[
 H^{\top}e_i=UA^{-\top}e_i,
 \qquad Ge_i=UAe_i,
\]
and hence the denominator above equals
\(\|H^{\top}e_i\|_2\|Ge_i\|_2\).  Taking the minimum over witness labels gives the lower bound \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\).  The declared formula for the printed \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)\) is instead the norm product itself; it is therefore not the reciprocal lower bound just derived.

Write \(i=I(m)\) for the latent target of intervention label \(m\).  The proof has six steps.

First, \(Y^{(0)}\) is a nondegenerate Gaussian vector in \(\mathbb R^n\), because \(A\) is invertible and every diagonal entry of \(\Omega_0\) is positive.  The matrix formed by \(n\) independent copies of \(Y^{(0)}\) has a joint Lebesgue density, and the zero set of its nonzero determinant polynomial is Lebesgue null.  Consequently the \(n\) corresponding observations \(X^{(0)}=UY^{(0)}\) span \(\mathcal S\) almost surely, so
\[
 \Pr_P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}})=1.
\]
The canonical-frame rule is a deterministic function of \(\mathcal S\), hence on this event it returns exactly \(U\).  The construction of \(\mathsf C\) expressly forbids inversion for \(r<r_0\).  Since \(N_{r_0}\ge n\), the same determinant argument shows that every \(S_{m,r}\), simultaneously over the finite environment set and countably many \(r\ge r_0\), is positive definite almost surely.  Thus every later inverse is well defined in the fixed space \(\mathbb R^n\).  When \(a_r>(2\kappa)^{-1}\), the corrected construction uses only vacuous intervals, so no decision is accepted before the deterministic inverse-perturbation premise is available.

Second, we construct the simultaneous covariance event.  For a fixed environment and stage put
\[
 W_{m,r}=\Sigma_m^{-1/2}S_{m,r}\Sigma_m^{-1/2}-I_n.
\]
For every fixed unit vector \(u\), the random variable
\(N_r u^{\top}(W_{m,r}+I_n)u\) has the \(\chi^2_{N_r}\) law.  Its moment generating function
\(\mathbb E e^{\lambda(\chi^2_N-N)}=e^{-\lambda N}(1-2\lambda)^{-N/2}\), together with Markov's inequality and optimization over \(0<\lambda<1/2\), gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\left|\frac{\chi^2_N}{N}-1\right|>
 2\sqrt{t/N}+2t/N\right)\le2e^{-t}.
\]
A maximal \(1/4\)-separated set on the Euclidean unit sphere has cardinality at most \(9^n\), by comparing disjoint radius-\(1/8\) balls with a radius-\(9/8\) ball.  It is a \(1/4\)-net.  For every symmetric \(W\), polarization of a maximizing Rayleigh quotient gives
\[
 \|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\max_{u\text{ in the net}}|u^{\top}Wu|.
\]
Using \(t=t_r\), taking the union over the net and the \(n+1\) environments, and using \(\|\Sigma_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa\), we obtain an event \(\mathcal C_r\) with
\[
 \Pr_P(\mathcal C_r^c)\le\alpha2^{-r-1},
 \qquad
 \max_{m\in\mathcal E}\|S_{m,r}-\Sigma_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le a_r.
\]
Independence between stages is unnecessary because the retained samples are nested.  A union bound and the geometric series show that
\[
 \mathcal C=\bigcap_{r\ge r_0}\mathcal C_r
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 \Pr_P(\mathcal C)\ge1-\sum_{r\ge r_0}\alpha2^{-r-1}\ge1-\alpha.
\]

Third, we record the population geometry.  Denote the latent density in environment \(m\) by \(p_m^Z\).  In latent coordinates, let \(b_i\) be row \(i\) of \(B^{(0)}\), supported on the parents of \(i\), and write
\(Z_i=b_i^{\top}Z+\epsilon_i\), with variances \(\omega_i>0\) and \(\widetilde\omega_i>0\) before and after intervention.  Cancellation of the unchanged causal conditionals in the likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \nabla_z\log\frac{p_m^Z(z)}{p_0^Z(z)}
 =-\frac{\epsilon_i}{\omega_i}b_i
 +\left(\frac{\epsilon_i}{\omega_i}-\frac{z_i}{\widetilde\omega_i}\right)e_i.
\]
The disturbance \(\epsilon_i\) is independent of its parental predictor.  If \(b_i\ne0\), that predictor has positive variance and the two displayed scalar coefficients have nonsingular covariance; if \(b_i=0\), variance reset \(\widetilde\omega_i\ne\omega_i\) makes the coefficient of \(e_i\) nondegenerate.  Score transformation under \(Y=AZ\) therefore proves
\[
 \operatorname{col}(R_m)=A^{-\top}\operatorname{span}\{e_i,b_i\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
For a set \(M\), the range of the positive-semidefinite sum is the span of the ranges in (1).

We now prove the population program's combinatorics.  If \(V\) is ancestral, then \(\operatorname{col}(R(V))=A^{-\top}\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in V\}\).  For \(k\in V\), if \(k\) is a leaf of the graph induced by \(V\), no vector \(b_i\), \(i\in V\setminus\{k\}\), contains coordinate \(k\), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}R(V\setminus\{k\})=|V|-1.
\]
If \(k\) is not a leaf, choose a remaining child \(c\).  The nonzero \(k\)-coordinate of \(b_c\), together with all target directions \(e_j\), \(j\ne k\), recovers \(e_k\) by subtraction; hence the rank is \(|V|\).  Removing a leaf preserves ancestry.  Induction shows that the smallest-label rank rule removes exactly the smallest labelled leaf at every step, and reversing the removal order gives the population topological order.

For the graph loop, the already recorded set \(D_t\) is descendant-closed by induction.  Thus
\(A_{t,j}=V_j\setminus D_t\) is ancestral and
\(M_{t,j}=A_{t,j}\setminus\{\pi_t\}\).  The preceding leaf calculation shows that \(\operatorname{col}(R(M_{t,j}))\) is either the dual-coordinate span indexed by \(M_{t,j}\), when \(\pi_t\) is a leaf in \(A_{t,j}\), or that indexed by all of \(A_{t,j}\), when it has a surviving child.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}projector\mbox{-}geometry}\) therefore says that the tested projector product is zero exactly in the latter case.  Updating \(D_t\) then records precisely the newly reached child and all of its already recorded descendants.  Induction on increasing \(j\), followed by decreasing \(t\), proves that the final graph is
\[
 \operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G_{\mathcal E})
 =I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I.
 \tag{2}
\]

Fourth, work on \(\mathcal C\) at a stage with \(a_r\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}covariance\mbox{-}to\mbox{-}correlation}\) gives, for every queried set \(M\),
\[
 b_M:=\|\widehat R_r(M)-R(M)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le |M|e_r.
 \tag{3}
\]
If \(b_M\le g_0/4\), Weyl's variational inequality and the band \(\{0\}\cup[g_0,\infty)\) certify the exact rank.  Let \(P_M\) be the population positive-range projector and \(\widehat P_M\) the empirical projector above \(g_0/2\).  Projecting the perturbed invariant-subspace equation onto \(\operatorname{null}(R(M))\) gives
\[
 \|P_M^{\perp}\widehat P_M\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{b_M}{g_0-b_M}.
\]
The certified ranks agree.  The principal-angle decomposition of two equal-rank orthogonal projectors, obtained by singular-value decomposition of their cross-Gram matrix, gives
\(\|\widehat P_M-P_M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|P_M^{\perp}\widehat P_M\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Consequently
\[
 \|\widehat P_M-P_M\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2b_M/g_0.
 \tag{4}
\]
The same bound holds for null projectors.  Let \(\widehat c_{t,j}\) denote the empirical projector-product norm corresponding to \(c_{t,j}(P)\).  For a graph comparison, (4) and the product triangle inequality imply
\[
 |\widehat c_{t,j}-c_{t,j}(P)|
 \le \frac{2(b_{V_t}+b_{M_{t,j}})}{g_0}
 \le\frac{4ne_r}{g_0}.
 \tag{5}
\]
If all previous certified decisions agree with the population transcript, the next query is an occurrence in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\).  Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}reached\mbox{-}eigen\mbox{-}band}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}reached\mbox{-}projector\mbox{-}band}\) are therefore applicable to that query.  Equations (3)--(5), the smallest-certified-zero rule, and induction through the restarted order and graph loops show that every completed empirical transcript equals the population transcript.  This is the required query-local induction; no promise is invoked for an unqueried subset.

Fifth, consider a certified singleton.  If \(e_r<g_0/2\), the same invariant-subspace calculation as above, now retaining its sharper denominator, gives
\[
 \|\widehat P_m-P_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{e_r}{g_0-e_r}.
\]
For the unit empirical vector \(\widehat v_m\), put
\(w_m=P_m\widehat v_m\) and \(v_m=w_m/\|w_m\|_2\).  It is defined and satisfies
\[
 \|\widehat v_m-v_m\|_2
 \le2\|(I-P_m)\widehat v_m\|_2
 \le\frac{2e_r}{g_0-e_r}\le\frac{4e_r}{g_0}.
\]
If \(e_r\ge g_0/2\), choose any unit \(v_m\in\operatorname{col}(R_m)\), which is nonempty by the variance-reset calculation (1); then the elementary bound between two unit vectors gives
\(\|\widehat v_m-v_m\|_2\le2\le4e_r/g_0\).  Thus the same bound holds at every certified stage.
Map both vectors into \(\mathcal S\) using the isometry \(U\), and stack the resulting rows as \(\widehat H\) and \(H^{\star}\).  Then
\[
 \|\widehat H-H^{\star}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|\widehat H-H^{\star}\|_{\mathrm F}
 \le4\sqrt n\,e_r/g_0.
 \tag{6}
\]
Each row of \(H^{\star}\) has unit norm and belongs to the required population singleton range.  By (1), if \(v_m=A^{-\top}q_m\), then \(q_m\) is supported on target \(i=I(m)\) and its parents, while
\[
 (v_m^{\top}U^{\top})G=v_m^{\top}A=q_m^{\top}.
\]
This is exactly the zero pattern in \(\mathrm{def{:}encoder\mbox{-}loss}\).  Hence (6) bounds \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H,P)\).

Finally, let \(b=b_{\star}\), \(q=q_{\star}\), and \(u=u_{\star}\), and let \(B=B_{\mathrm{samp}}=2^{r_B}\).  Since \(b\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\), one has \(q\ge256\), \(u>1\), and \(32qu^2\ge n\).  The power-of-two definition gives
\[
 32qu^2\le B<2\lceil32qu^2\rceil\le66qu^2.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 t_{r_B}=t_0+\log(2B)
 \le u+\log(132/16)+2\log u
 \le16u^2.
\]
It follows that
\[
 a_{r_B}
 \le4\kappa\left(\frac1{\sqrt{2q}}+\frac1{2q}\right)
 =\frac{b}{2\sqrt2}+\frac{b^2}{32\kappa}<b.
\]
Thus \(e_{r_B}<40\kappa^4b\le e_{\star}\).  In particular,
\[
 ne_{r_B}<g_0h_0/16\le g_0/16,
 \qquad
 4ne_{r_B}/g_0<h_0/4,
 \qquad
 4\sqrt n\,e_{r_B}/g_0<\tau.
\]
The rank intervals and comparison intervals therefore separate the two promised bands, and the corrected tolerance gate is also satisfied.  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}}\cap\mathcal C\), the procedure returns by this stage, (2) gives its graph, and (6) gives its encoder loss.  This event has probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  The sample accounting is exactly \(B_0=n+B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) observational samples, at most \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) in each intervention environment, and \(B_{\mathrm{tot}}=n+(n+1)B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) in total, as asserted.

Put \(\epsilon=2^{-n}\).  The structural coefficient matrix of \(\mathfrak F_n\) has nonzero rows only at \(3\) and \(4\), with parent vectors
\(b_3=(1,1)\) and \(b_4=(1,1+\epsilon)\); hence \(B^2=0\) and \(\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|B\|_{\mathrm F}<3\).  Every intervention deletes one row and has the same two properties.  Since
\((I-B)^{-1}=I+B\), and every intervention-noise covariance has spectrum in \([1,2]\),
\[
 \lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_m)
 \le2\|I+B^{(m)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2<32,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_m)
 \ge\|(I+B^{(m)})^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{-2}>1/16.
\]
Thus all observed covariances have spectrum in \([1/32,32]\).  The displayed equations also verify the linear Gaussian DAG, perfect single-target, variance-reset, and full-rank-mixing assumptions, with \(G=I_n\); independent samples may be drawn in each environment.

We next compute the primitive matrices.  A reset of a root gives
\(R_i=\tfrac14e_ie_i^{\top}\).  For a child with parent vector \(b\), write \(s=b^{\top}(Z_1,Z_2)\) and \(E=Z_c-s\).  Under the observational law, \(s\) and \(E\) are independent, and the score difference is
\[
 d_c=(-bE,(E-s)/2).
\]
Consequently, on the parent plane and coordinate \(c\),
\[
 R_c=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 bb^{\top}&-b/2\\
 -b^{\top}/2&(1+\|b\|_2^2)/4
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{col}(R_c)=\operatorname{span}\{b,e_c\}.
 \tag{7}
\]
In the orthonormal basis \(b/\|b\|_2,e_c\), writing \(B_0=\|b\|_2^2\in[2,5]\), the nonzero block has determinant \(B_0^2/4\) and trace \((5B_0+1)/4\).  Hence
\[
 \lambda_{min}^{+}(R_c)
 \ge\frac{\det(R_c|_{\operatorname{col}R_c})}
          {\operatorname{tr}(R_c|_{\operatorname{col}R_c})}
 =\frac{B_0^2}{5B_0+1}\ge\frac4{11},
\]
and therefore \(R_c\succeq(4/11)P_{\operatorname{span}\{b,e_c\}}\).

We claim that every nonempty subset of the four core labels other than \(\{3,4\}\) has positive eigenvalues at least \(1/40\).  Roots alone have gap \(1/4\), and a child alone has gap at least \(4/11\).  If a set contains one root \(i\) and a child with parent vector \(b\), then
\[
 \lambda_{min}^{+}
 \left(P_{e_i}+P_b\right)=1-|e_i^{\top}b|/\|b\|_2
 \ge1-2/\sqrt5>1/10.
\]
Multiplication by \(\min\{1/4,4/11\}=1/4\) gives a parent-plane lower bound strictly larger than \(1/40\), while the child coordinate has lower bound \(4/11\).  Adding the other child preserves these bounds and supplies its child coordinate; adding the other root gives the direct parent-plane bound \((1/4)I_2\).  These cases exhaust all core subsets other than \(\{3,4\}\).  Labels at least \(5\) contribute mutually orthogonal eigenvalues \(1/4\).

The population leaf order is
\[
 (3,4,1,2,5,6,\ldots,n),
\]
so the reversed order is
\(\pi=(n,n-1,\ldots,5,2,1,4,3)\).  In the first order round a queried deletion retains at least one core root whenever it retains both children; after label \(3\) is removed no later order query contains both children.  In a graph query containing both children, both core roots already belong to its prefix, descendant deletion removes no root, and deletion of the current row removes at most one root.  Singleton encoder queries contain only one child.  Thus no matrix occurrence has core intersection exactly \(\{3,4\}\), and the preceding case analysis proves that every reached positive eigenvalue is at least \(1/40\).

For graph queries, remove from a topological prefix the already recorded descendant-closed set.  The remainder is ancestral.  Removing the current label from that remainder leaves its coordinate absent when it is a leaf and supplied by a remaining child's parent vector otherwise, by (7).  Both queried ranges are therefore coordinate subspaces.  Their projector-product norm is consequently either zero or one.  Thus the reached projector band holds with \(h_0=1/2\).

The order phase has
\(\sum_{t=2}^n t=n(n+1)/2-1\) matrix occurrences.  The graph phase has \(n-1\) prefix occurrences and \(n(n-1)/2\) comparison-sum occurrences, and the encoder has \(n\) singleton occurrences.  Their sum is
\[
 n(n+1)/2-1+(n-1)+n(n-1)/2+n=n^2+2n-2.
\]

It remains to evaluate the unqueried margin.  The four vectors
\(e_3,b_3,e_4,b_4\) are independent because
\(\det(b_3,b_4)=\epsilon\ne0\), so \(R(\{3,4\})\) is positive definite on the four-dimensional core.  For
\(v=(1,-1,0,0)^{\top}/\sqrt2\), (7) gives
\[
 v^{\top}R_3v=0,
 \qquad
 v^{\top}R_4v=\epsilon^2/2.
\]
The Rayleigh variational principle therefore yields
\[
 \eta^{\ast}(P)
 \le\lambda_{min}^{+}(R(\{3,4\}))
 \le\epsilon^2/2=2^{-2n-1}<1/80.
\]
Since \(G=H=I_n\), the definitions give
\(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\), while
\(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\).

Finally, every Gaussian density and causal conditional is strictly positive and smooth.  Let \(\phi_v\) denote the centered Gaussian density of variance \(v\).  The intervention likelihood ratio for a root is a nonconstant ratio of centered Gaussian densities; for a child, differentiating the ratio
\(\phi_2(z_c)/\phi_1(z_c-b^{\top}z_{\mathrm{pa}(c)})\) in either parent coordinate gives a nonzero function because the corresponding entry of \(b\) is nonzero.  This verifies the stated parent-ratio condition.  Each covariance entry is an average of independent products having finite variance, so Chebyshev's inequality gives entrywise convergence in probability of \(S_{m,r}\) to \(\Sigma_m\), and finite dimension gives operator-norm convergence.  On the uniformly positive-definite neighborhood, the identity \(S^{-1}-\Sigma^{-1}=S^{-1}(\Sigma-S)\Sigma^{-1}\) gives \(S_{m,r}^{-1}\to\Theta_m\) in probability.  Multiplication by a Gaussian vector with finite second moment then gives convergence of the empirical linear score differences in squared \(P_0\)-mean in probability.  This is the stated score-difference consistency condition.  All defining assumptions of \(\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(1/40,1/2,32)\) and all listed non-margin source conditions have now been checked.

On the fixed-margin source region in the statement, equation (22), as recorded in \(\mathrm{def{:}source\mbox{-}margins}\), gives
\[
 \lambda_i(R(M))\in\{0\}\cup[g_0,\infty)
 \quad\text{for every }M\subseteq[n].
\]
In particular this holds for every matrix occurrence of \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\), so \(\mathrm{ass{:}reached\mbox{-}eigen\mbox{-}band}\) holds.  The separately imposed common actual-geometry condition is exactly \(\mathrm{ass{:}reached\mbox{-}projector\mbox{-}band}\).  The common linear Gaussian perfect-intervention hypotheses, observed conditioning, and independent sampling supply the remaining member properties in \(\mathrm{def{:}promised\mbox{-}class}\).  Hence
\[
 P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa).
\]
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}projector\mbox{-}geometry}\) independently shows that a comparison with witness label \(i\) is at least \(\rho_i(G)\); it does not replace the assumed actual-geometry band.  In particular the printed condition
\(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}<\gamma^{\ast}(G)\) cannot be inverted into a lower bound on \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\).

To prove strictness at \((g_0,h_0,\kappa)=(1/40,1/2,32)\), apply Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}separation\mbox{-}family}\).  It gives
\[
 \mathfrak F_n\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(1/40,1/2,32),
 \qquad
 \gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1,
 \qquad
 \eta^{\ast}(P)\le2^{-2n-1}<1/80.
\]
Thus \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\in(0,1)\), all listed non-margin source conditions and the actual projector band hold, but
\(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\notin(0,\eta^{\ast}(P))\).  The witness is outside the fixed-margin source region and inside the promised transcript-local class.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}promised\mbox{-}transcript\mbox{-}certificate}\) applies to it using only reached bands.  This establishes the asserted strict inclusion and, because the implication from the printed norm product to reciprocal projector geometry was nowhere used, also establishes the final noncontainment qualification.

At zero radius, every empirical matrix enclosure is the singleton containing its population matrix.  Hence a Weyl interval labels an eigenvalue zero exactly when the eigenvalue is zero and labels it positive exactly when it is positive.  The rank decisions of \(\mathsf C\) are therefore the rank decisions of \(\mathsf A\), and the smallest-certified-zero rule is exactly the public smallest-label rule.

Inductively suppose the two programs have made the same previous decisions.  They then form the same next sets \(V_t\), \(M_{t,j}\), and \(D_t\).  Their column- and null-space projectors are identical, so their projector-product norms and their zero decisions coincide.  The induction covers the order, graph, and singleton-range loops and proves equality of the complete environment-labelled transcript.

For completeness, the graph identified by that transcript is the causal closure rather than a graph defined by the procedure.  The Gaussian likelihood-ratio calculation gives
\(\operatorname{col}(R_m)=A^{-\top}\operatorname{span}\{e_{I(m)},b_{I(m)}\}\).  On an ancestral remaining set, removing a leaf lowers the range rank by one, whereas removing a nonleaf leaves its coordinate supplied by a remaining child's parent vector.  Thus the reverse removal order is topological.  In the graph loop, removing the current coordinate from the relevant descendant-pruned ancestral set leaves its dual coordinate in the comparison range exactly when it has a surviving child.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}projector\mbox{-}geometry}\) makes the corresponding product zero exactly in that case.  The descendant update therefore records, by induction, exactly all and only directed descendants.  Relabelling latent target \(I(m)\) by environment \(m\) yields
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal G}=\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G_{\mathcal E})
 =I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I.
\]

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Use \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sup}}\), the disjoint \(n\)-draw observational support batch, to recover its span; if that span has dimension below \(n\), return \(\bot\) without inversion.  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}}\), the span equals the deterministic support \(\mathcal S\), so apply the public canonical-frame rule to obtain exactly \(U\) and set \(Y_i^{(m)}=U^{\top}X_i^{(m)}\).  Maintain one retained post-support stream in each environment.  At stage \(r=0\), retain the first \(N_0=1\) observation from each stream; at every stage \(r\ge1\), append exactly \(N_r-N_{r-1}\) new observations, so the cumulative stream contains exactly \(N_r=2^r\) observations per environment.  For \(r<r_0=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\), sample and retain observations only; do not form an inverse or run any spectral or projector test. proposed.statement:
For any \(S,T\subseteq[n]\), all projectors below act on the fixed space \(\mathbb R^n\), and
\[
\left\|P_{\operatorname{span}\{A^{-\top}e_j:j\in T\}}P_{\operatorname{span}\{A^{-\top}e_j:j\in S\}^{\perp}}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T\subseteq S.
\]
For every witness label \(i\in T\setminus S\), the left-hand side is at least \(\rho_i(G)=1/(\|A^{-\top}e_i\|_2\|Ae_i\|_2)=1/(\|H^{\top}e_i\|_2\|Ge_i\|_2)>0\), and hence at least \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\).  The source's printed quantity \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\) is a norm product, not this reciprocal lower bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A complete Turing-model proof for certified invariant subspaces with repeated positive eigenvalues and for the adaptively composed projector-product norm intervals.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen primitives give operator gaps and exact-real perturbation bounds, but they do not provide a verified rational spectral-projector routine with explicit intermediate bit growth. A generic appeal to stable eigensolvers would not prove polynomial Boolean complexity or the required outward-rounding budget.
open_obligations.attempted: Rational perturbation bounds close covariance inversion, primitive formation, Weyl rank decisions, and the required working precision for those pieces. Polynomial-filter and contour-resolvent routes were considered, but neither has a declared theorem or a complete coefficient and rounding analysis in the frozen core.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The covariance-to-primitive part admits the following certified partial result.  If rational matrix centers have entrywise rounding radius at most \(2^{-p}\) and all matrices being inverted have smallest eigenvalue at least \((2\kappa)^{-1}\), then their operator perturbation is at most \(n2^{-p}\), the inverse perturbation is at most \(4\kappa^2n2^{-p}\), and the three-factor formula for each primitive matrix has perturbation at most \(C n\kappa^4 2^{-p}\) for an absolute rational constant \(C\).  Weyl intervals incur the same operator error.  Consequently covariance inversion, primitive formation, and all rank decisions can be certified with arithmetic error at most \(e_{\star}/8\) using
\[
 p=O\!\left(L+\log n+\log\kappa+\log(1/e_{\star})\right),
\]
and polynomially many Boolean operations.  This does not yet certify the repeated-eigenspace projectors and their adaptively composed product norms with the remaining \(e_{\star}/8\) budget.
